solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Conspiracy to nominate patient man

parts.note: to put up a candidate is to nominate them
Job, the biblical figure famed for his patience

explanation.surface: A plot to put forward someone known for his endless patience.
explanation.definitionFit: A put-up job is a scheme secretly arranged in advance, a rigged conspiracy.

clue.text: When trailing, place letters furthest apart in squares

indicators.note: trailing means coming behind, so this piece goes at the end

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street addresses
A and Z sit at opposite ends of the alphabet
as means when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: An instruction to lay out letters in a grid of squares as far apart as possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trailing' is the signal that the piece for 'When' goes last, though it comes first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Plazas are open public squares in a town, from the Spanish word.

clue.text: Bar bible in grave without success

indicators.note: in places the bible abbreviation inside the trimmed word
without means lacking, so the letter for success is dropped

parts.note: grave in the sense of serious or severe gives stern
S is a standard abbreviation for success
AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: A bible lies on a grave after a failed attempt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' looks like a burial place but is the adjective meaning serious; 'without' and 'in' are the signals that trim it and fill it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tavern is a pub or inn, a place serving drinks just as a bar does.

clue.text: Boundary with everyone chasing ball

indicators.note: chasing means following behind, so this piece goes after the others

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance party
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Everyone races after a ball until it hits the boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chasing' places 'everyone' at the end; a cricket reader may see the boundary rope, but here it is a wall between houses.
explanation.definitionFit: A party wall is the shared wall dividing two adjoining properties, forming the boundary between them.

clue.text: Where in France is academic institution mentioned briefly?

definitions.text: Where in France is academic institution mentioned briefly?

parts.words: Where in France is academic institution mentioned briefly?
parts.note: the French word for where is spelt the same as the two-letter short form of a British distance-learning university

explanation.surface: A question about where a French university is located.
explanation.walkthrough: French for 'where' is OU, which is also the usual abbreviation of the UK's distance-learning university.
explanation.definitionFit: The Open University is the British university teaching students remotely, commonly shortened to OU.

clue.text: Plastic alien is mine

parts.note: plastic in the sense of pliable or floppy gives limp
ET, the film's extraterrestrial, is the crossword's stock alien

explanation.surface: Someone declares that a plastic extraterrestrial toy belongs to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' reads as the possessive pronoun, but it is the explosive device.
explanation.definitionFit: A limpet mine is an explosive clamped magnetically to a ship's hull, so the shellfish name stands for the weapon.

clue.text: Move time to bury dead

indicators.note: move tells you to shift one letter to a new position in the word

parts.note: to inter is to bury

explanation.surface: A call to shift the schedule so the deceased can be buried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Move' shifts T in INTER to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Inert means lifeless or motionless, so it fits dead in the sense of showing no activity.

clue.text: Write about match in the shade

indicators.note: about means around, so the pen word wraps the other

parts.note: a pen is what you write with, and to pen is to write
to agree is to match, as accounts that tally

explanation.surface: Writing an article about a football match while sitting in the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the wrapping signal; 'match' reads as a game but means to correspond.
explanation.definitionFit: Pea green is a bright yellowish-green colour, one particular shade.

clue.text: Model employee found dead

parts.note: a temp is a temporary employee
the late someone is someone deceased

explanation.surface: A worker who modelled has been found dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A template is a pattern or model from which copies are made.

clue.text: Duck meals: you might get this depressed

definitions.text: Duck meals: you might get this
definitions.meaning: eating a duck could leave a little of its fluffy feathers on your tongue

explanation.surface: A diner warns that eating duck leaves fluff on the tongue and makes you glum.
explanation.definitionFit: Being down in the mouth means looking miserable or dejected, a synonym of depressed.

clue.text: Hostile publicity campaign wastes time and energy

indicators.note: to waste something is to lose it, so the letter for time drops out of the word

parts.note: a run of adverts makes up a publicity campaign
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An aggressive advertising push squanders time and effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wastes' removes T from ADVERTS, leaving ADVERS, and E is then added.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverse conditions or comments are unfavourable and antagonistic, a synonym of hostile.

clue.text: How to throw wild prom rave — not quietly!

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters running out of control into a new order
not before quietly says that the quiet letter is to be left out of the fodder

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Advice on how to throw a raucous school dance party, but loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quietly' drops P from PROM to leave ROM; 'wild' then rearranges ROM plus RAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Overarm describes bowling or throwing with the arm brought over the shoulder, a manner of delivery.

clue.text: Rig up a sound beam

indicators.note: sound tells you to go by how the words are said aloud rather than spelt

parts.note: a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: Instructions to set up a sonic beam device.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'a ray' runs together into one word; the spoken RAY is written with a doubled R once joined to A.
explanation.definitionFit: To array is to arrange or dress up, which is what rigging something up means.

clue.text: To ignore odd characters running at thug really is artificial

indicators.note: skipping the first, third, fifth letters and so on leaves only the even ones of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Disregarding the strange people charging at a ruffian is genuinely unnatural behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd characters' sounds like strange people, but it means letters in odd positions; the even letters of 'running at thug really' remain.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unnatural is not produced by nature, a close synonym of artificial.

clue.text: Do we all owe this as a result of a bet?

definitions.text: Do we all owe this as a result of a bet?

parts.words: Do we all owe this as a result of a bet?
parts.note: the money the whole country owes, playfully reread as a gambling debt run up on the Grand National horse race

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about whether a whole nation is in hock from a wager.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the National' is the Grand National, the famous steeplechase that the whole country bets on.
explanation.definitionFit: The national debt is the total sum a country's government owes, which notionally all citizens share.

clue.text: Ambush initial deployment, surrounding both flanks

indicators.note: deployment is the rearranging of forces in the field, so the letters are redeployed

parts.note: east and west are the two flanks on a map, giving E and W

explanation.surface: An ambush where the first deployment of troops encircles the enemy on both wings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounding' fits the surface picture: the two flank letters E and W end up inside the redeployed letters of INITIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie in wait is to hide ready to attack, which is what an ambush is.

clue.text: Carte blanche for secretaries to have fun

parts.note: PAs are personal assistants, secretaries
sport means fun or amusement, as in 'make sport of'

explanation.surface: Unlimited freedom for office secretaries to enjoy themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A passport, figuratively, is a guaranteed means of access, like free rein or carte blanche.

clue.text: Woman plays guitar in The Police

parts.note: she is a woman
a guitarist riffs, playing short repeated phrases

explanation.surface: A woman plays guitar in the rock band The Police.
explanation.walkthrough: The Police looks like the band, but it means law officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheriffs are law officers in US counties, part of the police.

clue.text: Hell lies with each catastrophic vulnerability

indicators.note: a catastrophic outcome leaves things in ruin, so the letters are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: Hell and falsehoods combine into each person's disastrous weak spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catastrophic' rearranges the twelve letters of HELL, LIES and EACH.
explanation.definitionFit: A weak spot named after the Greek hero whose heel was the only place he could be wounded.

clue.text: Tart caught by police in middle of road

indicators.note: by means beside, so caught stands next to the rest
in the middle of says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the A1 is Britain's longest numbered road, written AI in crosswords
the CID is the detective branch of British police
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A loose woman is arrested by police in the middle of the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in middle of' and 'by' are the placing signals; 'Tart' looks like a noun but is the adjective meaning sour.
explanation.definitionFit: Acidic means sharp or sour to the taste, just as tart does.

clue.text: What many people say is that very old version of Windows works — almost

parts.note: XP was a version of Microsoft Windows

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: ops are works, as in an opus and its plural

explanation.surface: A claim that an outdated computer operating system mostly works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims OPS to OP.
explanation.definitionFit: Vox pop, from Latin vox populi, is a recorded sample of public opinion: the voice of the people.

clue.text: Virus stores fuel dump contents in seaweed

indicators.note: stores means holds inside, so one piece is kept within the other

parts.note: SARS is the respiratory virus
gas is a fuel

indicators.note: the contents of a word are its inner letters, without the outer pair

explanation.surface: A virus contaminates fuel stores and the dump's contents in the seaweed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stores' signals one piece kept inside another, and 'contents' takes only the inner letters of the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sargassum is a genus of floating brown seaweed that gives the Sargasso Sea its name.

clue.text: Some bare naked characters featured in amphitheatre

indicators.note: some says only part of the following words' letters is used
letters featured inside the phrase make up the answer

explanation.surface: Nudity on show in a Roman amphitheatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took 'characters featured in amphitheatre', but those first words are the hidden-word signal; the definition is just 'amphitheatre'.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is the central stage of an amphitheatre, and the word names the whole venue.

clue.text: Not available to chop end off chip

indicators.note: taking the end off a word removes its final letter

explanation.surface: A kitchen note: if it can't be had, cut the end off the chip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end off' cuts the last letter from CHOP, leaving CHO.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacho is a tortilla chip, typically baked with cheese as a Tex-Mex snack.

clue.text: Unusual to be away on journey

parts.note: to be off is to be away or gone
a beat is a regular round or route travelled, like a police officer's

explanation.surface: It is unusual to be off travelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Offbeat describes something unconventional or eccentric, a synonym of unusual.

clue.text: In speech, you criticise political party for winning on this

indicators.note: in speech says the word is taken by how it is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: the pronoun is said exactly like the letter U
to pan is to criticise harshly
the DUP is Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party

explanation.surface: Someone speaking about attacking a political party to get votes.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the phrase 'on the up-and-up', meaning on a winning streak: you are 'on this' when winning.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the up-and-up means steadily improving or succeeding, the condition of someone who keeps winning.

clue.text: Italian you French run over

parts.note: tu is the French familiar word for you
to scan a text is to run one's eyes over it

explanation.surface: An Italian and a French person get into a road accident.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tuscan is a native of Tuscany, the region of central Italy, so an Italian person.

clue.text: A mountain has one wave

definitions.meaning: a snowy peak wears a pale crown of snow
a breaking sea wave with foam on its crest

explanation.definitionFit: A whitecap is a wave with a foaming crest, and figuratively a snowy summit on a mountain.
